subject: science
prompt_en: Compare a maize (makka) leaf and a hibiscus leaf. How are their veins different, and what does that tell you about their roots?
prompt_hi: Makke ki patti aur gudhal ki patti compare karo. Nasein kaise alag hain, aur isse jadon ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
answer: Maize has parallel veins, so fibrous roots; hibiscus has net-like veins, so a tap root.

subject: science
prompt_en: A banana leaf has long veins running side by side from the middle rib to the edge. What root type do you expect?
prompt_hi: Kele ki patti mein beech ki nas se kinare tak lambi nasein ek ke baaju ek chalti hain. Kaun si jad expect karoge?
answer: Fibrous roots.

subject: science
prompt_en: We eat the root of a radish (mooli), and we also cook its leaves. Do you think mooli leaves have net-like or parallel veins? Explain.
prompt_hi: Mooli ki jad hum khaate hain aur patton ki sabzi bhi banti hai. Tumhe kya lagta hai, mooli ke patton mein jaal jaisi nasein hongi ya seedhi parallel? Samjhao.
answer: Net-like (reticulate), because a radish is a tap root, and plants with tap roots usually have net-like venation.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw two leaves, one with net-like veins and one with parallel veins. Under each, draw the root that usually goes with it.
prompt_hi: Do pattiyan banao, ek jaal jaisi nason wali aur ek parallel nason wali. Har ek ke neeche woh jad banao jo usually uske saath hoti hai.
answer: Net-veined leaf with a tap root (one main root with side roots); parallel-veined leaf with fibrous roots (a bunch of thin roots).

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu wrote: 'Grass has parallel veins, so it has a tap root.' Check Golu's sentence.
prompt_hi: Golu ne likha: 'Ghaas mein parallel nasein hain, isliye uski tap root hai.' Golu ka vaakya check karo.
answer: Wrong pairing: parallel veins go with fibrous roots, so grass has fibrous roots.

subject: science
prompt_en: Teach your little brother the 'leaf tells the root' trick, with one example of each kind.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote bhai ko 'patti batati hai jad' wali trick sikhao, dono tarah ka ek-ek example dekar.
answer: Key ideas: net-like veins usually mean a tap root (e.g. mango, tulsi, mustard); parallel veins usually mean fibrous roots (e.g. grass, wheat, maize); this is true for most plants.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: an onion has many thin roots coming out of its bottom. What type of roots are these?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: pyaaz ke neeche se bahut saari patli jadein nikalti hain. Ye kis type ki jadein hain?
answer: Fibrous roots.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why is grass, with its fibrous roots, good at holding soil on a slope during heavy rain?
prompt_hi: Tez baarish mein dhalaan pe mitti ko pakad ke rakhne mein ghaas, apni fibrous jadon ki wajah se, achhi kyon hai?
answer: Its many thin roots spread through the top soil like a net and hold the soil particles together, so rain cannot wash the soil away easily.

subject: science
prompt_en: Name two features of a camel and say how each helps it live in the desert.
prompt_hi: Oont ki do khoobiyan batao aur har ek registaan mein kaise madad karti hai.
answer: Any two: long legs keep its body away from the hot sand; wide padded feet don't sink into sand; it can go many days without drinking water; long eyelashes keep sand out of its eyes; it can close its nostrils against sand; its hump stores fat for energy.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: a cactus and a money plant are both not watered for three weeks in a hot place. Which will still look healthy, and why?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: cactus aur money plant dono ko garam jagah pe 3 hafte paani nahi diya. Kaun sa abhi bhi theek dikhega, aur kyon?
answer: The cactus: its thick fleshy stem stores water, and spines instead of broad leaves and a waxy coat cut down water loss.

subject: science
prompt_en: A deodar or pine tree in the hills is shaped like a cone with sloping branches. Predict what happens to heavy snow falling on it, compared with a wide, flat-topped tree.
prompt_hi: Pahaadon ka deodar ya cheed ka ped cone jaisa hota hai, jhuki hui daaliyon wala. Guess karo, uspe bhaari barf giregi toh kya hoga, ek chaude sapaat chhat wale ped ke mukaable?
answer: Snow slides off the sloping branches of the cone-shaped tree, so the branches don't break; on a wide flat-topped tree snow piles up and branches can break.

subject: science
prompt_en: Pour a few drops of water on a lotus leaf or an arbi (colocasia) leaf from the market. Predict what the water will do.
prompt_hi: Kamal ki patti ya bazaar se laayi arbi ki patti pe paani ki kuch boondein daalo. Guess karo, paani kya karega?
answer: The water forms round drops that roll off, because the leaf's surface is waxy and water-repelling; the leaf stays dry.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why can't a fish live on land, even if you give it plenty of food?
prompt_hi: Machhli ko kitna bhi khana do, woh zameen pe kyon nahi reh sakti?
answer: It breathes with gills, which take in oxygen dissolved in water; out of water its gills cannot work, so it cannot breathe. Its fins are for swimming, not walking.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare a fish and a frog. Both can swim, but a frog can also live on land. What features let each do this?
prompt_hi: Machhli aur medhak compare karo. Dono tair sakte hain, par medhak zameen pe bhi reh sakta hai. Kaun si khoobiyan dono ko ye karne deti hain?
answer: Fish: gills, fins and a streamlined body, so it lives only in water. Frog: lungs (and moist skin) to breathe air, strong back legs for jumping and webbed feet for swimming, so it lives on land and in water.

subject: science
prompt_en: A snow leopard lives high in the Himalayas. Guess two features it might have that help it there.
prompt_hi: Snow leopard Himalaya mein bahut oonchaai pe rehta hai. Do khoobiyan guess karo jo wahan uski madad karti hongi.
answer: Any two: thick fur for warmth; wide furry paws that work like snowshoes; a long thick tail to wrap around itself and for balance; colouring that blends with rocks and snow.

subject: science
prompt_en: In hot summers people in Delhi wear loose cotton clothes, and in Ladakh people wear thick woollen layers. How is this like an adaptation, and how is it different?
prompt_hi: Delhi mein garmi mein log dheele cotton ke kapde pehente hain, aur Ladakh mein moti woollen layers. Ye adaptation jaisa kaise hai, aur alag kaise?
answer: Like: it helps people cope with the conditions. Different: people choose and change clothes quickly, while an animal's adaptations are body features it is born with, which developed over many generations; it cannot take them off.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a camel and label three features that help it in the desert, with a few words on how each helps.
prompt_hi: Ek oont banao aur 3 khoobiyan label karo jo registaan mein madad karti hain, har ek ke saath kuch shabd ki kaise madad karti hai.
answer: Any three, e.g.: long legs, keep away from hot sand; padded feet, don't sink; long eyelashes, keep sand out; hump, stores fat.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'The camel wanted to store water, so it grew a hump full of water.' Find the two mistakes.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Oont paani jama karna chahta tha, isliye usne paani se bhara koohad uga liya.' Do galtiyan dhundho.
answer: 1) The hump stores fat, not water. 2) Animals don't grow features because they want them; adaptations developed over many generations.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your friend what an adaptation is, using one desert, one cold and one water example.
prompt_hi: Apne dost ko samjhao adaptation kya hota hai, ek registaan, ek thandi jagah aur ek paani ka example dekar.
answer: Key ideas: an adaptation is a feature that helps a living thing survive in its habitat; desert: cactus spines and fleshy stem or camel's padded feet; cold: yak's thick hair or cone-shaped pine trees; water: fish gills and fins or lotus floating waxy leaves; adaptations developed over many generations.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what is the special word for features that help a living thing survive in its habitat?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jo khoobiyan kisi jeev ko apne habitat mein jeene mein madad karti hain, unke liye khaas shabd kya hai?
answer: Adaptations.

subject: science
prompt_en: What job does a vulture do in nature?
prompt_hi: Prakriti mein giddh kya kaam karta hai?
answer: It eats dead animals (carcasses), cleaning up the surroundings and reducing the spread of disease.

subject: science
prompt_en: A village's frogs all disappear because their pond was filled with soil. Predict what happens to the insects there, and to the snakes that eat frogs.
prompt_hi: Ek gaon ka talaab mitti se bhar diya gaya aur saare medhak gayab ho gaye. Guess karo, wahan ke keedon ka kya hoga, aur medhak khaane wale saanpon ka?
answer: Insects that frogs eat, such as mosquitoes, may increase; snakes that eat frogs have less food and may become fewer or move away.

subject: science
prompt_en: India lost most of its vultures. Predict what happened to dead cattle lying in the open, and to the number of stray dogs.
prompt_hi: Bharat mein zyada-tar giddh khatam ho gaye. Guess karo, khule mein pade mare hue jaanwaron ka kya hua, aur aawara kutton ki sankhya ka?
answer: Carcasses lay rotting for longer, and stray dogs fed on them, so the number of stray dogs went up, raising the risk of dog bites and rabies.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said stray dogs increased when vultures declined. Why is that dangerous for people?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha giddh kam hue toh aawara kutte badh gaye. Ye logon ke liye khatarnaak kyon hai?
answer: More dogs means more dog bites, and dogs can spread rabies, a deadly disease; rotting carcasses also spread germs and smell.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare a natural forest with a plantation of a single kind of tree. Which has more diversity, and why does that matter?
prompt_hi: Ek prakritik jungle aur sirf ek tarah ke pedon ka plantation compare karo. Kis mein zyada vividhta hai, aur ye kyon zaroori hai?
answer: The natural forest; its many kinds of plants give many kinds of food and homes for many animals, and if one species is lost, others can still keep the web going.

subject: science
prompt_en: In some places farmers sprayed so much insect poison that bees and butterflies became rare. What could happen to their fruit and vegetable crops?
prompt_hi: Kuch jagah kisaanon ne itna keetnaashak chhidka ki madhumakkhiyan aur titliyan bahut kam ho gayin. Unki phal aur sabzi ki fasal ka kya ho sakta hai?
answer: Fewer pollinators means fewer flowers are pollinated and become fruits, so the harvest of crops like mango, pumpkin and mustard falls.

subject: science
prompt_en: Many Indian villages protect 'sacred groves' (devrai, devban, kavu) where nobody cuts trees. How does this help biodiversity?
prompt_hi: Bharat ke kai gaon 'sacred groves' (devrai, devban, kavu) bachate hain jahan koi ped nahi kaatta. Isse vividhta ko kaise madad milti hai?
answer: The grove keeps a patch of natural forest safe, so many native plants, birds, insects and other animals survive there; it also protects springs and acts as a source of seeds for the area.

subject: science
prompt_en: Turn this into a chain with arrows: grass is eaten by deer, and deer are eaten by tigers. Then tell me what happens to the tigers if the deer disappear.
prompt_hi: Isse teer wali chain mein badlo: ghaas ko hiran khaata hai, aur hiran ko baagh. Phir batao agar hiran gayab ho jaayein toh baaghon ka kya hoga.
answer: Grass → deer → tiger. Without deer, tigers lose their main food, so they go hungry, become fewer, move away or may attack village cattle.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'Earthworms and vultures are useless creatures. We should only protect tigers and peacocks.' What would you tell Golu?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Kenchue aur giddh bekaar jeev hain. Hume sirf baagh aur mor bachane chahiye.' Tum Golu ko kya bataoge?
answer: Every species has a role: earthworms loosen soil and make it fertile; vultures clean up carcasses. Losing them harms other living things, including people.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain the vulture story to your parents and what it teaches us about diversity.
prompt_hi: Apne mummy-papa ko giddh wali kahani samjhao aur batao isse vividhta ke baare mein kya seekh milti hai.
answer: Key ideas: cattle were given the painkiller diclofenac; vultures eating their carcasses died; carcasses rotted, stray dogs increased and rabies risk rose; lesson: species depend on each other, so losing one affects many, including humans; harmful chemicals must be stopped and species protected.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: name two things people can do to protect the variety of living things around us.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: do kaam batao jo log apne aas-paas ki vividhta bachane ke liye kar sakte hain.
answer: Any two: protect forests and other habitats; don't pollute ponds and rivers; plant native trees; avoid harmful pesticides and drugs that poison wildlife; don't hunt or capture wild animals; keep water for birds in summer; protect sacred groves.

subject: science
prompt_en: Which nutrient helps a child grow and repairs a cut or wound?
prompt_hi: Kaunsa poshak tatva bachche ko badhne mein aur chot ya ghaav bharne mein madad karta hai?
answer: Proteins.

subject: science
prompt_en: Sort these foods by the main nutrient they give: rice, dal, ghee, guava, roti.
prompt_hi: In khaanon ko unke mukhya poshak tatva ke hisaab se baanto: chawal, dal, ghee, amrood, roti.
answer: Rice: carbohydrate. Dal: protein. Ghee: fat. Guava: vitamins (especially vitamin C) and fibre. Roti: carbohydrate (and fibre if whole wheat).

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: which has more protein, a bowl of cooked moong dal or a bowl of plain cooked rice of the same size?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: same size ki katori mein, pakki moong dal mein zyada protein hai ya saade pake chawal mein?
answer: The moong dal; pulses are rich in protein, while rice is mainly carbohydrate.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: which gives far more vitamin C, one amla from the local market or one imported packaged apple?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: local bazaar ka ek amla ya ek imported packed seb, kisme kahin zyada vitamin C hai?
answer: The amla; it is one of the richest sources of vitamin C, much richer than an apple, and it is cheap and local.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said dal gives protein. Why does a growing child need protein every day?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha dal se protein milta hai. Badhte bachche ko roz protein kyon chahiye?
answer: Proteins are body-building nutrients: the body uses them to make and repair muscles, skin, blood and other parts, and a child's body is growing every day.

subject: science
prompt_en: Ghee and sugar both give energy. How are they different as nutrients?
prompt_hi: Ghee aur cheeni dono energy dete hain. Poshak tatva ke roop mein dono alag kaise hain?
answer: Ghee is a fat and sugar is a carbohydrate; fats give about twice as much energy per gram, and fats also help the body use some vitamins.

subject: science
prompt_en: Think of your school mid-day meal, such as khichdi with vegetables. Which nutrients does it give?
prompt_hi: Apne school ke mid-day meal ke baare mein socho, jaise sabzi wali khichdi. Isse kaun-kaun se poshak tatva milte hain?
answer: Rice gives carbohydrates; dal gives protein; vegetables give vitamins, minerals and fibre; oil or ghee gives fat; and it contains water.

subject: science
prompt_en: A cricket coach plans meals for players during a tournament. Why should the plan include more than just energy foods?
prompt_hi: Ek cricket coach tournament ke dauraan khiladiyon ka khaana plan karta hai. Plan mein sirf energy waale khaane se zyada kyon hona chahiye?
answer: Players need carbohydrates and fats for energy, proteins to repair and build muscles, vitamins and minerals to stay healthy and recover, water to replace sweat, and fibre for digestion.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw your thali as a circle and colour each part by what it mainly does: energy food, body-building food or protective food. Describe your thali to me.
prompt_hi: Apni thali ko ek circle mein banao aur har hisse ko rang do ki woh mainly kya karta hai: energy, body-building ya protective. Phir mujhe apni thali batao.
answer: For example: roti or rice = energy (carbohydrates); dal or curd = body-building (protein); sabzi, salad or fruit = protective (vitamins, minerals, fibre); a little ghee = energy (fat).
